image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on water with golden-yellow ripples. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow-orange bill, and a grey/brown body. It is positioned in profile facing right.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellow-orange hue consistent with the 'yellow-green' description for this species.
The eye is visible as a small, dark spot on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and greyish-brown body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing a broad structure that tapers towards the tail, consistent with a pointed wing shape when folded.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short and black. While the specific 'curl' of the central feathers is subtle due to the angle and water line, the general morphology of a short, upright tail is present.
